source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Unit 2 (PDF 27-38, printed 22-33); not printed in the book. Based on the unit's text, theorems, formulas and worked examples (changed values); none repeats the unit's exercises. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Unit 2 (Functions and Graphs), arranged by the unit's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation that shows the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The term function was introduced by the mathematician:
blocks.explanation: The unit states that the German mathematician Leibniz (1646-1716) introduced the term function.

book_ref.quote: The term function was introduced by the German mathematician Leibniz

blocks.prompt: 2 The volume of a sphere is \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\). For \(r = 6\), \(V =\)
blocks.explanation: \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi(6)^{3} = \frac{4}{3}\pi(216) = 288\pi\); one radius gives only one volume.

book_ref.quote: of a sphere depends on its radius

blocks.prompt: 3 Which of the following is NOT allowed for a function?

options.text: two inputs having the same output
some elements of the second set not used
every input having exactly one output

blocks.explanation: Each element of the first set must correspond to one and only one element; two inputs may share an output.

book_ref.quote: each element in the first set corresponds to one and only one element in the second set

blocks.prompt: 4 For a function \(f : X \to Y\), the set \(X\) is called the:
blocks.explanation: The set \(X\) of inputs is the domain of \(f\); \(Y\) is the co-domain.

book_ref.quote: The set \(X\) is called the domain of \(f\).

blocks.explanation: \(f(1) = 2\), \(f(2) = 4\), \(f(3) = 6\); the range is the outputs that occur, \(\{2, 4, 6\} \subseteq Y\).

book_ref.quote: The set of corresponding elements

blocks.prompt: 6 The range of a function is always:
blocks.explanation: The range is the actual set of outputs, so it is always a subset of the co-domain.

book_ref.quote: So the range is always a subset of the co-domain.

blocks.prompt: 7 Which rule from \(X = \{1, 2, 3\}\) to \(Y = \{p, q\}\) is a function?
blocks.explanation: Every element of \(X\) must have exactly one image. Only the first rule does this; the others leave an input out or give \(1\) two images.

book_ref.quote: is a rule or a correspondence that assigns to each element

blocks.text: 2.1.2 Notation and Value of a Function

blocks.prompt: 8 The notation \(y = f(x)\) was invented by:
blocks.explanation: The Swiss mathematician Euler (1707-1783) wrote \"\(y\) is a function of \(x\)\" as \(y = f(x)\).

book_ref.quote: invented a symbolic way to write the statement

blocks.prompt: 9 In \(y = f(x)\), the variable \(x\) is called the:
blocks.explanation: \(x\) is the independent variable (we choose it); \(y\) is the dependent variable.

book_ref.quote: is called the independent variable of
is called the value of \(f\) at \(x\)
the image of \(x\) under \(f\)

blocks.prompt: 12 If \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\), then \(f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\), \(x \ne 0\), is:

book_ref.quote: takes an input \(x\), operates on it in some way and produces exactly one output

blocks.prompt: 13 The domain of \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 3}\) is:
blocks.explanation: The denominator \(x - 3 = 0\) at \(x = 3\), where \(f\) is not defined; every other real \(x\) works.

book_ref.quote: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} - 4}\).

blocks.prompt: 14 The domain of \(f(x) = \frac{x + 1}{x^{2} - 25}\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} - 25 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm 5\); remove these. (\(x = -1\) only makes \(f = 0\), which is allowed.)

book_ref.quote: Domain: where is the denominator zero?

blocks.prompt: 15 The domain of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x - 4}\) is:
blocks.explanation: Need \(x - 4 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x \ge 4\); \(x = 4\) gives \(\sqrt{0} = 0\), so the end is included.

book_ref.quote: Condition for a real square root

blocks.prompt: 16 The range of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), is:
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 3 \ge 3\), and \(3 = f(0)\) is reached; every \(y \ge 3\) is reached by \(x = \sqrt{y - 3}\).

book_ref.quote: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = x^{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 17 The domain of \(f(x) = \sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\) is:
blocks.explanation: Need \(16 - x^{2} \ge 0\). Critical points \(\pm 4\); testing \(x = 0\) gives True, \(x = \pm 5\) False; ends included.

book_ref.quote: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} - 9}\).

blocks.prompt: 18 The set of all \(x\) with \(-2 \le x < 5\) is written as:
blocks.explanation: \(-2\) is included (square bracket), \(5\) is not (round bracket).

book_ref.quote: In a closed interval \([a, b]\) the endpoints are included.

blocks.prompt: 19 The range of \(f(x) = -x^{2}\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), is:
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow -x^{2} \le 0\); \(0 = f(0)\) is reached and every \(y \le 0\) comes from \(x = \sqrt{-y}\).

book_ref.quote: Every real number can be squared

blocks.prompt: 20 By the vertical line test, a graph represents a function if and only if:

options.text: no horizontal line meets the graph more than once
every vertical line meets the graph twice
no vertical line meets the graph more than once
the graph passes through the origin

blocks.explanation: A graph is a function if and only if no vertical line intersects it more than once.

book_ref.quote: A graph represents a function if and only if no vertical line intersects the graph more than once.

blocks.prompt: 21 Which of these graphs is NOT the graph of a function of \(x\)?
blocks.explanation: The line \(x = 0\) meets the circle at \((0, 4)\) and \((0, -4)\): one input, two outputs.

book_ref.quote: If any vertical line passes through the graph more than once, it is not a function.

blocks.prompt: 22 The vertical line \(x = 1\) meets the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 10\) at:
blocks.explanation: \(1 + y^{2} = 10 \Rightarrow y^{2} = 9 \Rightarrow y = \pm 3\): two points, so the circle is not a function of \(x\).

book_ref.quote: The vertical line test is a method used to determine whether a graph represents a function.

blocks.prompt: 23 A function \(f\) is one-to-one if:

options.text: every element of the co-domain has a pre-image

blocks.explanation: One-to-one: different inputs give different outputs, i.e. \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2}) \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\).

book_ref.quote: A function \(f\) is one-to-one if different inputs produce different outputs

blocks.prompt: 24 Which function \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) is one-to-one?

book_ref.quote: This means that no two different elements of the domain map to the same element of the co-domain.

blocks.prompt: 25 For \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = 3x - 6\), the pre-image of \(9\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(3x - 6 = 9 \Rightarrow x = 5\); check \(f(5) = 9\).

book_ref.quote: has at least one pre-image in the domain

blocks.prompt: 26 \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\) is not onto, because which element of the co-domain has no pre-image?
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} = -1\): no real root. (\(1, 2, 5\) come from \(x = 0, \pm 1, \pm 2\).)

book_ref.quote: for every \(y\) in \(Y\), there exists an \(x\) in \(X\) such that

blocks.prompt: 27 A function is called bijective if it is:
blocks.explanation: Bijective \(=\) one-to-one and onto.

book_ref.quote: is called bijective if it is both one-to-one and onto.

blocks.prompt: 28 The function \(f(x) = x^{2}\) from \(\mathbb{R}\) to \([0, \infty)\) is:
blocks.explanation: Every \(y \ge 0\) has the pre-image \(\sqrt{y}\) (onto), but \(f(2) = f(-2) = 4\) (not one-to-one).

book_ref.quote: if every element in the co-domain

blocks.explanation: \(1 \ge 1\), so use the second piece: \(f(1) = 1^{2} + 2 = 3\). (\(2\) comes from the wrong piece.)

book_ref.quote: A piecewise function is a function that is defined by different expressions
Each piece applies to a specific part of the domain.

blocks.prompt: 31 For \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^{2} - 5\), the range is:
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} - 5 \ge -5\), reached at \(x = 0\); so \(f\) is not onto \(\mathbb{R}\).

book_ref.quote: Show that the function \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\), where the domain and co-domain are all real numbers, is neither one-to-one nor onto.

blocks.prompt: 32 Which pair of inputs shows that \(f(x) = x^{2} + 4\) is not one-to-one?
blocks.explanation: \(f(3) = f(-3) = 13\): two different inputs, same output.

book_ref.quote: Show that the function \(f(x) = x + 1\), where the domain and co-domain are all real numbers, is bijective.

blocks.prompt: 33 The point of intersection of the graphs of two functions represents:

options.text: the solution of the two equations together

blocks.explanation: A point on both graphs satisfies both equations, so it is a solution of the system.

book_ref.quote: This point represents the solution(s) to the equations of the given functions.

blocks.text: 2.2.1 Intersection of a Linear Function and Coordinate Axes

blocks.prompt: 34 The line \(y = 3x - 12\) meets the \(x\)-axis at:

book_ref.quote: Find the points of intersection of a linear function

blocks.prompt: 35 The line \(y = -4x + 7\) meets the \(y\)-axis at:

book_ref.quote: While the coordinate axes refers to

blocks.prompt: 36 Which of these is a linear function?
blocks.explanation: In a linear function the highest power of the variable is one: \(5 - 2x\).

book_ref.quote: linear function is a function in which the highest power of the variable is one

blocks.prompt: 37 The lines \(y = 2x + 1\) and \(y = -x + 7\) intersect at:
blocks.explanation: \(2x + 1 = -x + 7 \Rightarrow 3x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 2\), \(y = 5\). Both lines pass through \((2, 5)\).

book_ref.quote: The point of intersection of two linear functions is the point where their graphs cross each other.

blocks.prompt: 38 How many points of intersection do \(y = 4x + 1\) and \(y = 4x - 3\) have?
blocks.explanation: Same slope \(4\), different intercepts: the lines are parallel. \(4x + 1 = 4x - 3\) gives \(1 = -3\), impossible.

book_ref.quote: This means the two functions have the same

blocks.prompt: 39 A table gives \(y = x + 2\): \(2, 3, 4\) and \(y = -x + 4\): \(4, 3, 2\) for \(x = 0, 1, 2\). The point of intersection is:
blocks.explanation: At \(x = 1\) both columns give \(3\), so \((1, 3)\) is on both lines.

book_ref.quote: By plotting the above points, we see that

blocks.text: 2.2.3 Intersection of a Linear Function and a Quadratic Function

blocks.prompt: 40 A line and a parabola can intersect in at most:
blocks.explanation: They meet at two points, one point or not at all; the combined equation is a quadratic with at most two real roots.

book_ref.quote: A line and a parabola can either intersect at two points, one point or not intersect at all.

blocks.prompt: 41 The vertex of the parabola \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 1\) is:

book_ref.quote: The vertex \((h, k)\) of the parabola

blocks.prompt: 42 The line \(y = 2x - 1\) and the parabola \(y = x^{2}\) meet at:
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} = 2x - 1 \Rightarrow (x - 1)^{2} = 0\): one point \((1, 1)\); the line is a tangent.

book_ref.quote: suggesting that the line may be tangent to the parabola

blocks.prompt: 43 How many points do \(y = x\) and \(y = x^{2} + 2\) have in common?
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} - x + 2 = 0\) has discriminant \(1 - 8 = -7 < 0\): no real root, so no intersection.

book_ref.quote: If no solution exists, it means the line and the parabola do not intersect.

blocks.prompt: 44 The points of intersection of \(y = x + 1\) and \(y = x^{2} - 1\) are:

book_ref.quote: If there are two solutions, the system has two points of intersection.

blocks.prompt: 45 The \(x\)-intercepts of \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 1\) are at \(x =\)

blocks.text: 2.3 Graph of the Square Root Function

blocks.prompt: 46 The domain of \(y = 3\sqrt{x} - 2\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt{x}\) is real only for \(x \ge 0\); the \(3\) and \(-2\) do not change this.

book_ref.quote: as the square root of a negative number is not a real number

blocks.prompt: 47 The range of \(y = 3\sqrt{x} - 2\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt{x} \ge 0 \Rightarrow 3\sqrt{x} - 2 \ge -2\), reached at \(x = 0\).

book_ref.quote: Graph the square root function

blocks.prompt: 48 The graph of \(y = 2\sqrt{x} + 3\) starts at the point:
blocks.explanation: Smallest allowed \(x\) is \(0\): \(y = 2\sqrt{0} + 3 = 3\).

book_ref.quote: Table values and the graph of the function are given below:

blocks.prompt: 49 For \(y = 3\sqrt{x} + 1\), the value of \(y\) at \(x = 4\) is:

book_ref.quote: Plot the points of the table and join them with a smooth curve

blocks.prompt: 50 The domain of \(y = \sqrt{x - 2}\) is:
blocks.explanation: Need \(x - 2 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x \ge 2\).

book_ref.quote: Clearly the domain of \(y = 2\sqrt{x} + 1\) is \(x \ge 0\)

blocks.text: 2.4 Graph of the Cube Root Function

blocks.prompt: 51 The domain of \(y = \sqrt[3]{x + 5}\) is:
blocks.explanation: The cube root of any real number (positive, negative or zero) is real, so every real x is allowed.

book_ref.quote: because the cube root of any number (positive, negative or zero) is always real

blocks.explanation: \((-3)^{3} = -27\), so \(\sqrt[3]{-27} = -3\); negative numbers have real cube roots.

book_ref.quote: The range of the given function is also the set of real numbers.

blocks.prompt: 53 The graph of \(y = \sqrt[3]{x + 2}\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at:
blocks.explanation: \(y = 0 \Rightarrow x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2\); the graph of \(\sqrt[3]{x}\) moved \(2\) units left.

book_ref.quote: Graph the cube root function

blocks.prompt: 54 For \(y = \sqrt[3]{x - 1}\), the value of \(y\) at \(x = 9\) is:

book_ref.quote: As we know that cube root function is defined for all real numbers

blocks.prompt: 55 Which of these is an example of decay?

options.text: money in a bank account earning interest
a population of rabbits increasing over months
a radioactive substance losing its strength over years

blocks.explanation: Decay: a quantity decreasing over time, e.g. a radioactive substance or cooling coffee.

book_ref.quote: When something decreases in quantity or size over time, it is called decay.

blocks.prompt: 56 In \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\), the value at \(t = 0\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(P(0) = P_{0}e^{0} = P_{0}\): the starting value.

book_ref.quote: The value of a stock follows the exponential growth model

blocks.prompt: 57 A quantity grows as \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{0.07t}\). Its doubling time is about:

book_ref.quote: After how many years will the stock double in value?

blocks.prompt: 58 A stock worth Rs. 2,000 grows as \(P(t) = 2000e^{0.04t}\). After 5 years its value is about:

book_ref.quote: Find the value of the stock after 10 years.

blocks.prompt: 59 A concentration is \(C(t) = \frac{60}{\sqrt{t + 4}}\) ppm. \(C(5) =\)

book_ref.quote: The concentration of a pollutant in a lake

blocks.prompt: 60 For \(C(t) = \frac{60}{\sqrt{t + 4}}\), the concentration becomes exactly \(10\) ppm when \(t =\)
blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt{t + 4} = 6 \Rightarrow t + 4 = 36 \Rightarrow t = 32\); after that \(C\) is below \(10\).

book_ref.quote: After how many days will the concentration drop below 10 ppm?
